item.title: Sports events fuel China's holiday tourism, consumption
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
Various sports events are being held across China during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays as part of broader efforts to boost holiday tourism and consumption. YINCHUAN, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- Engines roared at the foot of Helan Mountain in northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region on Thursday, as more than 700 drivers and riders from across the country competed in an off-road race on the first day of the seven-day National Day holiday. The seventh Helan Mountain Auto and Motorcycle Off-Road Race, which began on Sept. 30 in Shizuishan City, Ningxia, will run through Oct. 6 along an 80-kilometer route through the Gobi Desert and canyons. The event is part of broader efforts to leverage sporting events to attract visitors and stimulate holiday consumption. As one of 23 major sporting events being held in Ningxia from mid-September through the end of October, this event spans the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. Ningxia, known for its wine industry, has issued online wine consumption vouchers worth three million yuan (447,000 U.S. dollars) and offered discounts on local tourist attractions for visitors with sports event tickets. During the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, the Eastern Foothill of Helan Mountain Half Marathon, held in Yinchuan on Sept. 26, attracted 5,500 runners from more than 10 provincial-level regions. The route passed vineyards and wineries, while post-race activities included wine tasting, vintage tram tours of local wineries, food fairs and open-air concerts. Local authorities are also seeking to turn event-related visitor traffic into longer stays and broader spending. In Shizuishan, the former coal-mining town of Shitanjing, now an industrial heritage tourism site, has attracted visitors alongside local markets and other attractions. Last year's off-road race recorded nearly 300,000 visits and generated about 15 million yuan in spending on catering, accommodation and retail, according to local authorities. "Riding past the wineries, I could smell the ripening grapes, and I plan to visit nearby scenic spots after the race. Events like this offer a good way to experience Ningxia," said Zhang Kun, a cyclist from Xi'an who took part in the inaugural Eastern Foothill of Helan Mountain Wine Cycling Open in late August which attracted 1,815 riders from 21 provincial-level regions. Similar efforts to weave sports into tourism and consumption are also taking place elsewhere in China during the holidays. In Anshan, northeast China's Liaoning Province, a Liaoning City Football League match drew 40,623 spectators on the night of the Mid-Autumn Festival. Ticket holders were also offered free admission to scenic spots and free rides on public transport. In Yuanling County, central China's Hunan Province, the International Canoe Federation Dragon Boat World Cup, held from Sept. 25 to 27 during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, brought together 24 teams from 16 countries and regions. "The World Cup's return to the birthplace of dragon boat racing is not only a sporting event but also a cultural homecoming," said Luk Wai-hung, Chairman of the International Canoe Federation's Dragon Boat Committee. In Qinhuangdao, north China's Hebei Province, more than 50 sporting events are being held during the two holidays. An ILCA-class Asian Cup sailing event has generated more than 13 million yuan in related consumer spending, according to local authorities. China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism launched a cultural and tourism consumption campaign on Sept. 22, featuring more than 20,000 activities and more than 310 million yuan in consumption vouchers. China's General Administration of Sport has promoted its "Travel with Sports Events" initiative under the National Fitness Plan (2026-2030), encouraging the integration of sports with tourism and other forms of consumption. "We will further integrate sports, culture, tourism and consumption, leveraging holiday periods to promote the initiative and turn sports-event traffic into stronger tourism and consumption growth," said Ai Yu, an official with China's General Administration of Sport. ■

item.title: Asian Games | China captures two climbing golds
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
NAGOYA, Japan, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- China claimed two sport climbing gold medals at the 2026 Asian Games on Thursday, with Zhang Yuetong winning the women's boulder title and Chu Shouhong triumphing in the men's speed event. In the women's boulder final, Zhang scored 85.0 points to edge Japan's Ai Mori by just 0.2 points. Zhang completed each of the first three problems on her first attempt, earning 25 points on each, before scoring 10 points on the fourth. Mori took silver with 84.8 points, while South Korea's Seo Chae-hyun claimed bronze with 70.0. China's Luo Zhilu finished fourth. "I was anxious for quite a long time before the competition because I was thinking too much. Today, I focused more on making adjustments and keeping my attention on myself," Zhang said. Zhang said she would have preferred more difficult problems that offered greater opportunities to separate the competitors. "The first two problems were not challenging enough for me and my teammates. We were more eager to see problems that could create a gap and allow us to demonstrate our competitive level," she added. In the men's speed final, Chu clocked 4.714 seconds to secure gold. Iran's Reza Shenazandi Fard finished second in 5.362, while Kazakhstan's Damir Toktarov took bronze in 7.342. False starts played a significant role in the men's competition. China's Long Jianguo and Japan's Ryo Omasa were both disqualified for false starts in the semifinals, while Indonesia's Tri Aditya Syahrial also missed out the podium after a false start. "The false starts by my opponents made me more nervous. I couldn't settle my breathing while standing, so I sat down to calm myself, regulate my breathing and stay focused," Chu said. "Technique accounts for 60 to 70 percent, while focus accounts for 30 to 40 percent. The two complement each other and neither can be missing," he added. Chu said winning on China's National Day made the victory particularly significant. "I feel that the strength given to me by my country helped me win this gold medal. Winning it on such a special day makes it especially meaningful to me," he said. ■

item.title: China's Shenzhou-23 astronauts send National Day greetings from space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-23 astronauts aboard China's Tiangong space station sent video greetings to their motherland on Thursday, which is China's National Day and the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. Commander Zhu Yangzhu and his crewmates Zhang Zhiyuan and Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered their wishes for the country and its space program together as the station, about 400 km above Earth, flew over China. "When we look at Earth from the space station, that brilliantly lit land is the motherland we miss day and night," said Li, the first astronaut from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region to travel to space. The three astronauts were launched aboard the Shenzhou-23 spaceship late on May 24 and have been in orbit for more than four months. They are in good condition, having completed in-orbit crew rotation with the Shenzhou-21 astronauts, repaired the station's solar panels in a spacewalk and deployed application payloads outside the station. This year marks the 70th anniversary of the founding of China's space program. Remarkable milestones include the launch of the country's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System that offers global services, the Chang'e lunar missions, the Tianwen-1 Mars mission, the Tiangong space station and the steady advance of crewed lunar exploration project. "We can never forget that in deserts, mountains and on islands, a group of people have gazed at the stars and kept striving, generation after generation, for 70 years, creating the glory of China's space program," said Zhang, who is on his first spaceflight. Zhu, from China's third batch of astronauts, is on his second spaceflight after the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, and is commanding a long-duration mission for the first time. "The 'baton of history' has been passed to us. We will certainly run this leg well, and keep safeguarding and building our home in space," he said. ■

item.title: China's high-speed rail network expansion to facilitate cross-city collaboration
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- China's newly opened high-speed railway sections will help promote cross-city collaboration and closer regional economic ties, boosting the flow of talent, technology and capital across regions, experts said. On Monday, China opened four major high-speed railway sections spanning northern, northwestern, central and northeastern regions. This move further expands the world's largest high-speed rail network, enhancing connections between major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country. "The opening of the four lines will promote industrial transformation and upgrading and cross-regional industrial transfer, boost the development of resources along the routes, and inject new momentum into coordinated regional economic and social development," said Yuan Baohua, deputy director of the construction department of China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. Each of the four new sections helps bind regions closer together. The Xiong'an-Shangqiu section, for instance, tightens ties between Xiong'an New Area and central-southern Hebei, southwestern Shandong and eastern Henan, while the Harbin-Yichun line extends the two-hour transportation circle centered on Harbin in northeast China, Yuan said. As the rail network turns from isolated lines into an interconnected web, regional cooperation is deepening, according to Ma Botao with the China Railway Economic Planning and Research Institute. Ma said the expanding network is bringing cities and city clusters much closer together. Commuting within metropolitan areas now takes about one hour, living and working across city clusters about two hours, and business travel between neighboring city clusters and provincial capitals around three hours. "The railway network closely binds large and small cities, making industrial division of labor and cross-city employment the norm," he said. The benefits of the network extend beyond the areas directly along the new lines. For instance, the Yichang-Xingshan section narrows the time-space distance not just between the two cities, but between the Chengdu-Chongqing region and the city cluster in the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, Ma said. The new lines also provide direct support for key national strategies. Noting that the Xiong'an-Shangqiu section fills the gap in Xiong'an New Area's southbound high-speed rail corridor, Liu Yanhong, deputy general manager of Xiong'an high-speed railway corporation, said that the line facilitates commuting and business exchanges for relocated enterprises and institutions, and supports stronger industrial cooperation along the route. For cities newly connected to the network, seizing the opportunity depends on how well they position themselves. "Generally, large cities focus on research and development, finance and headquarters economy, while small cities should leverage their local agriculture, ecology, tourism and distinctive industrial strengths to undertake supporting manufacturing, agricultural product processing, and wellness and cultural tourism, serving as both industrial supporting bases and leisure backyards for central cities," Ma said. To turn transport advantages into real development gains, Ma advised cities to strengthen connections between high-speed rail stations and industrial parks as well as major population clusters, and improve housing and public services for talent. China is home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, with more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail in operation by the end of 2025. Under national plans, the network is projected to expand to 70,000 km by 2035, connecting major cities, city clusters and key economic zones throughout the country. ■

item.title: Chinese celebrate 77 years of People's Republic, advance modernization with confidence
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-01
BEIJING, Oct. 1 (Xinhua) -- Hours before dawn on Thursday, Tian'anmen Square was already alive with anticipation. More than 100,000 people from across China gathered at the heart of Beijing to watch the national flag-raising ceremony as the People's Republic of China (PRC) marked its 77th founding anniversary. At around 6:10 a.m., the national anthem echoed across the square. People sang in unison, their eyes following the five-starred red flag as it rose into the sky. For many, the moment brought tears. When a large flock of white doves soared into the air, cheers and applause erupted from the crowd, filling the square with jubilation. Children waved national flags as they ran about, young people chatted and laughed with national flag stickers on their cheeks, and older visitors in bright, festive clothes smiled for group photos in front of an 18-meter-high flower basket at the center of the square. The festive mood extended far beyond the capital. Across the country, many streets were lined with national flags and floral displays, while residential communities were adorned with lanterns and traditional Chinese knots. "Every time I pass these flower displays, I feel inspired," said Gao Feng, a food delivery rider who crossed Chang'an Avenue, a major thoroughfare through central Beijing. "I truly believe that if everyone does their job well and takes things one step at a time, we can build a better future," Gao said. On Wednesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other senior leaders paid tribute to fallen heroes at a Martyrs' Day ceremony, honoring those who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the PRC. China also presented the 2026 Chinese Government Friendship Award to 50 foreign experts in recognition of their contributions to China's development and to friendship and cooperation between China and other countries. REMARKABLE PROGRESS On this very day 77 years ago, the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong stood on Tian'anmen Rostrum and declared the birth of the PRC, marking a watershed moment in Chinese history. In the decades since, China has risen from a poor country to the world's second-largest economy and a major country striding toward the center of the world stage. By 2025, China's GDP had surpassed 140 trillion yuan (about 19.6 trillion U.S. dollars), accounting for about one-sixth of global GDP, while the country continued to contribute roughly 30 percent of global economic growth. Economic growth has translated into higher incomes and longer lives. Per capita disposable income rose from just 49.7 yuan in 1949 to 43,377 yuan in 2025, while average life expectancy more than doubled, from 35 years to 79.25 years. The country has eliminated absolute poverty and established the world's largest systems for education, social security and healthcare. Over the past decades, China has undergone one of the world's largest and fastest urbanization processes. Once largely agrarian, China is now home to about twice as many urban residents as rural residents. China has become a global manufacturing powerhouse, producing everything from new-energy vehicles to industrial robots and advanced chips. In 2025, output of new-energy vehicles exceeded 16 million units, while production of industrial robots and integrated circuits rose by 28 percent and 10.9 percent, respectively. It has emerged as one of the world's fastest-rising forces in innovation, making major advances in cutting-edge fields such as artificial intelligence, biomedicine and quantum technology. It has achieved breakthroughs in both land-based and sea-based rocket recovery technologies. These changes have also shaped the way China engages with the wider world. More people around the world are gaining a deeper appreciation of an increasingly innovative and culturally vibrant China through firsthand encounters. At the same time, its experience has broadened the paths for developing countries to achieve modernization. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, said at a reception on the eve of the National Day. JOURNEY AHEAD For visitors, the giant flower basket at the heart of Tian'anmen Square is a backdrop for holiday photos. And far more than that, it tells a story about where China is heading. This year marks the beginning of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, which runs from 2026 to 2030. The basket features 15 types of floral designs and five types of fruit, symbolizing hopes for abundant blossoms and fruitful results over the next five years. Beyond the flower basket, 10 three-dimensional flower installations line Chang'an Avenue, bringing themes such as new quality productive forces, harmony between people and nature, urban renewal and beautiful rural areas to life. Together, they highlight some of China's development priorities for the next five years. Those priorities are backed by concrete goals. The plan aims to lay the groundwork for doubling per capita GDP from its 2020 level by 2035, while accelerating breakthroughs in core technologies in key fields. It also calls for raising average years of schooling among the working-age population to 11.7 years and life expectancy to 80 years, while further strengthening China's soft power. The 15th Five-Year Plan period represents a crucial window for laying a solid foundation toward China's 2035 goal of basically achieving socialist modernization and making decisive progress in that direction. The plan has dedicated sections on Hong Kong and Macao, outlining measures to support the two regions in better integrating into and contributing to the country's overall development. In September, Hong Kong unveiled its first Five-Year Plan, while Macao released its third in August, both aligned with the national development strategy. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has maintained progress despite pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development while demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, Xi said at Wednesday's reception. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great PRC," Xi added. ■

item.title: Xi pays tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping straightens the ribbon on a flower basket during a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. Xi Jinping and other leaders of the Communist Party of China and the state including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the ceremony on Wednesday. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders attended a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning. The event was held to mark Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. Since Martyrs' Day was established in 2014, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day. The other leaders who attended the ceremony on Wednesday included Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng. They were joined by representatives from all walks of life. At 10 a.m., all attendees sang the national anthem, followed by a moment of silence in tribute to the heroes who sacrificed their lives for the liberation of the Chinese people and the development of the People's Republic of China. Nine large flower baskets were placed in front of the Monument to the People's Heroes. Xi and other leaders walked up to the foot of the monument, where he straightened the ribbons on the baskets. Then, they walked around the monument to pay their tributes. The baskets, with ribbons reading "Eternal Glory to the People's Heroes," were presented in the name of the CPC Central Committee; the National People's Congress Standing Committee; the State Council; the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference; the Central Military Commission; non-Communist parties, the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce, and patriots without party affiliations; people's organizations and people from all walks of life; veterans, retired senior officials and the relatives of martyrs; and Chinese Young Pioneers. Yin Li, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and secretary of the CPC Beijing Municipal Committee, presided over the ceremony. This year marks the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC and the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the Communist Party of China and the state including Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attend a ceremony to present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. item.title: Xi calls for firm confidence, solid steps for China's national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech at a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Sept. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on the nation to forge ahead with firm confidence and take solid steps to achieve the great national rejuvenation. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a reception held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. China's National Day falls on Oct. 1. Li Qiang presided over the reception. Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attended the event along with around 800 guests. "The great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is unstoppable," Xi said. "As long as we remain confident, stay focused on our goals and move forward steadily, step by step, success will ultimately belong to the great CPC, the great Chinese people and the great People's Republic of China." He noted that over the past 77 years, the Party has led the Chinese people in achieving two miracles: rapid economic growth and enduring social stability. "We take immense pride in the extraordinary achievements of New China and have full confidence in the bright prospects of Chinese modernization," he said. Since the beginning of this year, the Chinese economy has continued to progress despite mounting pressure and achieved innovation-driven and high-quality development, demonstrating strong resilience and vitality, he said. Efforts should be made to sustain this momentum, promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development, take practical steps to safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, and meet the targets and tasks set for the year, so as to ensure a good start to the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), he said. Xi stressed the need to remain firmly committed to the policy of "one country, two systems," under which the people of Hong Kong administer Hong Kong, the people of Macao administer Macao, and both regions enjoy a high degree of autonomy. He went on to say that the central government will support Hong Kong and Macao in integrating more fully into the country's overall development. The central government is committed to maintaining their long-term prosperity and stability, Xi added. He also called for efforts to deepen exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait, resolutely fight secessionist forces seeking "Taiwan independence," oppose external interference, and promote the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations to advance national reunification. China will stick to its independent foreign policy of peace, advance the implementation of the four major global initiatives it proposed, and promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity to contribute greater certainty and positive energy to a turbulent world, Xi said. ■ The Communist Party of China and state leaders Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang, Li Xi and Han Zheng attend a reception to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China along with around 800 guests at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)
